dom.push.connection.enabled.why: Background connections nobody asked for: off Region lookup by IP address Updates of Mozilla's system add-ons (Whisper updates as a whole) Media plugins (OpenH264 for WebRTC video, Widevine for DRM video) still download on first start as in Firefox, but from the list built into Whisper (with SHA-512 of each file) instead of asking Mozilla's update server (aus5.mozilla.org) first. The address below is never reachable, so Firefox goes straight to that list. Web push: no permanent connection to Mozilla's push server (push.services.mozilla.com). Sites cannot send notifications while they are closed.

dom.reporting.header.enabled.why: Code execution and network hardening PDF files open without running their JavaScript. Add-ons only from the profile and from Whisper itself (5 = profile + application): nothing a program drops into a user or system extension folder is loaded. No 0-RTT early data: a network attacker could replay it (TLS 1.3 and HTTP/3). A sub-resource from another site cannot pop up a login prompt (1: only from the same site as the page). Pages do not make the browser send reports to servers the page chose: no CSP violation reports, no Reporting API deliveries. Pages behave the same (the securitypolicyviolation event still fires); only the outgoing request is gone.

Without a click on the page nothing opens, the same as for a blocked scheme. ms-* schemes to ask about instead of blocking, comma separated (e.g. "ms-teams"). Ask before an add-on starts a program through native messaging. Windows schemes Firefox itself does not block, stopped before any JavaScript runs as well (the guard above blocks them too; this is the second lock).

security.OCSP.enabled.why: Code execution and network hardening PDF files open without running their JavaScript. Add-ons only from the profile and from Whisper itself (5 = profile + application): nothing a program drops into a user or system extension folder is loaded. No 0-RTT early data: a network attacker could replay it (TLS 1.3 and HTTP/3). A sub-resource from another site cannot pop up a login prompt (1: only from the same site as the page). Pages do not make the browser send reports to servers the page chose: no CSP violation reports, no Reporting API deliveries. Pages behave the same (the securitypolicyviolation event still fires); only the outgoing request is gone. No OCSP: an OCSP request tells the certificate authority which site you are about to open. Revocation of public web certificates is checked on this device with CRLite (from Remote Settings), which Firefox 159 already prefers over OCSP for them; OCSP answers stapled by the site itself are still used. What is lost: revocation checks for certificates from roots you added yourself (company or private CAs).

Wallet extensions are not affected.

whisper.security.seedguard.pause_after_w.why: Recovery phrase guard (WhisperInputGuardChild.sys.mjs) A wallet recovery phrase (12-24 words of an official BIP39 list with a valid checksum, or an Electrum seed) typed, pasted or dropped into a web page is stopped before the page receives it, with a warning; holding a button for 3 seconds allows that one field. Wallet extensions are not affected. While typing, the field is paused after this many complete words that are all from one list (0: only the whole phrase is stopped). At 6 of 12 words the rest cannot be guessed; ordinary text starts with 6 list words in about 1 field in 8,700.
